Check that criteria only refer to columns present in the data

Source: R/check-criteria.R
check_criteria.Rd

A pre-flight check run before any step is evaluated. For every step in criteria, the variables used by a formula predicate, the by column(s) and the arms column must exist in data. If any are missing, check_criteria() aborts with one line per offending step, naming the step number, its label and the missing column(s), instead of letting evaluation fail later with object 'x' not found.

Usage

check_criteria(criteria, data)

Arguments

criteria

A cf_criteria object.

data

A data frame.

Value

NULL, invisibly. Called for its side effect of aborting when a criterion refers to a column not in data.

Details

apply_criteria() and continue_criteria() call this automatically (after the expected / join step, so joined columns count as present). Call it directly to validate a criteria set against a dataset without applying it.

What is checked

Variables in a formula predicate count as present when they are a column of data, or when they resolve in the formula's environment (e.g. a local min_age <- 18 used as ~ age >= min_age), matching how predicates are evaluated. A consequence is that a missing column whose name matches an object on the search path (e.g. c or t) is not reported, because evaluation would find that object too. The dplyr helpers n(), n_distinct(), cur_group() and cur_group_id() and the .data / .env pronouns are always allowed; .data$x is checked as column x. Function names, pkg::fn references and the right-hand side of obj$field are not treated as columns.

Function predicates cannot be inspected statically and are skipped (their by / arms columns are still checked); the error message notes which steps were skipped.

See also

apply_criteria(), continue_criteria().

Other criteria builders: cf_criteria(), cf_criterion(), exclude(), group_exclude(), group_include(), include(), randomise(), select_within()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 50, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Adults only") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consent recorded")
check_criteria(crit, dat)   # passes silently

# A column that is not in the data is reported with its step
bad <- crit |> exclude(~ lost_to_follow_up, label = "Lost to follow-up")
try(check_criteria(bad, dat))
#> Error in .check_criteria(criteria, data) : 
#>   Criteria refer to column(s) not found in `data`.
#> ✖ Criterion 3 "Lost to follow-up" refers to column(s) not in data: lost_to_follow_up.
